DESIGN SPEC — a controlled photographic material study of unequal arrival:
Use case: ads-marketing. Asset type: one final flat opaque portrait poster, edge-to-edge, 2:3; no mockup, borders, panels, contact sheet or additional image. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Concept: Under the same gravity, different materials take different time to arrive. Make this relationship the large, unmistakable physical scene, independently legible even with the title hidden. Two similar unmarked transparent glass pouring vessels tip simultaneously from the upper corners, their pouring lips at the same height around the upper fifth. The left vessel contains clear thin water; the right contains dense amber syrup. The bodies may be deliberately cropped by the upper outer edges, but both rims, openings, actual liquid exit points and the vessels' coherent glass walls must remain readable. No hands or unrelated props. Do not render isolated floating luxury objects.

A front view slightly above a single matte pale gray receiving tabletop. The tabletop is physically visible across the lower fifth, with clear contact and consistent perspective. Both pours descend all the way from their vessel lips to this same receiving surface. At the left quarter, water accelerates down a clear narrow irregular continuous stream and strikes the surface into an energetic broad crown splash, a few physically related droplets, outward ripples and an extensive shallow transparent pool spreading across much of the left half. At the right three-quarter position, viscous honey-colored syrup is still drawing from the lip into one long connected stretching neck: thick near the vessel, narrowing continuously downward, then contacting a much smaller compact slow mound/puddle on the tabletop. It has smooth tension, broad restrained specular highlights, a rounded contact fold and deep translucent amber thickness. No discontinuous levitation, detached syrup blobs, giant syrup splash or equal-sized pools. The difference in descent and accumulation is the main shape, not decorative small droplets. Preserve enough separation between the water and syrup arrivals that their unequal extent is evident.

Photography and finish: tightly staged credible studio material study, pale cool gray field, a soft directional light from upper left shared by the two vessels and both liquids. Glass has fine coherent rims and restrained reflections, transparent water has sharp refractive highlights and thin edges, syrup has smooth thick amber tension and larger highlights. Avoid uniformly glossy surfaces, chrome, artificial mist, motion blur, copied grain, heavy gradients, wallpaper texture or generic product-ad glow. Render the impacts' contact shadows, pooling thickness and local reflections consistently. The subject action occupies most of the height and substantial width.

Typography is integrated into the irregular interval between the two vertical pours: print the title once as a substantial three-line whole-word group reading downward:
서로
다른
속도
These line breaks substitute only the two original word spaces; retain the words intact and in this exact order. Clean, measured charcoal-black sans-serif Hangul, normal square syllable proportions, open internal counters and even optical spacing. No liquid-shaped glyphs, stretching, condensed letters or 3D type. Put the group around the central middle third, approximately from 38% to 64% height, with steady generous line spacing, strong readable weight and a width about one quarter of the poster. The whole-word lines can gently follow the varying interval while remaining a coherent vertical reading. The title connects the tilted vessels above to the unequal arrivals below; it is not a header, caption or footer. No stream, splash, droplet, glass reflection or highlight may cross a letter or closely trap a syllable. Maintain a visible quiet clearance at every title edge.

Only the three words of the supplied title may appear in the poster. No punctuation, quote marks, measurements, vessel labels, arrows, watermarks, numbers, brand marks, technical notation, supporting copy or duplicated title. All design instructions and role identifiers are internal and must not be printed.
